 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:center" id="toc462861_11">SURF AIR&#8217;S MANAGEMENT&#8217;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">References in this section to the &#8220;Company&#8221;, &#8220;Surf Air&#8221;, &#8220;we&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221; refer to Surf Air Global Limited and its consolidated subsidiaries, which includes SAM. Unless otherwise indicated, all dollar amounts are set forth in thousands, except share and per share data. </span></p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">The following discussion and analysis is intended to help the reader understand Surf Air&#8217;s results of operations and financial condition. This discussion and analysis is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, the section entitled &#8220;Unaudited Pro Forma Condensed Combined Financial Information&#8221; and Surf Air&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included elsewhere in this prospectus. Some of the information contained in this discussion and analysis or set forth elsewhere in this prospectus, including information with respect to Surf Air&#8217;s plans and strategy for Surf Air&#8217;s business, includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Surf Air&#8217;s actual results may differ materially from management&#8217;s expectations as a result of various factors, including but not limited to those discussed in the sections entitled &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; and &#8220;Special Note&#160;Regarding Forward-Looking Statements&#8221;. </span></p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Overview of the Surf Air Business </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air is expanding the category of regional air travel, connecting underutilized regional airports and private terminals with high frequency &#8220;commercial-like&#8221; air service, using small turboprop aircraft. Surf Air operates primarily in California, and its model is based on its optimization of scheduled routes to meet its customers&#8217; demand. Surf Air currently provides a regional air mobility platform with scheduled routes and <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights operated by third-party Part&#160;135 operators and it intends to develop hybrid-electric and fully-electric powertrain technology with its commercial partners to electrify existing fleets, which it believes will reduce operating costs and emissions, starting with a hybrid-electric and a fully-electric variant of the Cessna Grand Caravan EX, one of the most prolific family of aircraft in the single engine turboprop category with approximately 3,000 aircraft in use worldwide. Surf Air&#8217;s customers consist of regional business and leisure travelers. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air generates revenue through the sale of membership products, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-member</span> single seats, or flight products for both scheduled and <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> flights. Scheduled revenue is derived from membership subscriptions, principally relating to two main categories of membership: All You Can Fly (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">AYCF</span>&#8221;) and Pay As You Fly (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">PAYF</span>&#8221;). AYCF membership subscriptions allow members to fly as much as they like over the contract period. The membership fee includes access to scheduled service and the cost of single seat booking. PAYF members pay a membership fee, which enables them to purchase single use vouchers for travel. <span style="white-space:nowrap">On-demand</span> service allows customers to book private charter flights on routes specified by the customer. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Internal Reorganization </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On July&#160;21, 2023, as contemplated by the Agreement and Plan of Merger and defined as the &#8220;Internal Organization&#8221; in the final prospectus and registration statement, dated July&#160;25, 2023 (the &#8220;Registration Statement&#8221;) and filed on July&#160;25, 2023 with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;), SAGL Merger Sub Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Surf Air Mobility (&#8220;SAM&#8221; or &#8220;the Registrant&#8221;), was merged with and into Surf Air, after which Surf Air became a wholly-owned subsidiary of SAM (the &#8220;Internal Reorganization&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to the Internal Reorganization, all ordinary shares of Surf Air outstanding as of immediately prior to the closing, were canceled in exchange for the right to receive shares of SAM Common Stock and all rights to receive ordinary shares of Surf Air (after giving effect to the conversions) were exchanged for shares of SAM Common Stock (or warrants, options or RSUs to acquire SAM Common Stock, as applicable) at a ratio of 22.4 Surf Air shares to 1 share of SAM Common Stock. Such conversions, as they relate to the ordinary shares of Surf Air, and all rights to receive ordinary shares, have been reflected as of all periods presented herein. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">73 </p>

</div></div>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>



<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On July&#160;25, 2023, SAM&#8217;s Registration Statement on <span style="white-space:nowrap">Form&#160;S-1</span> and <span style="white-space:nowrap">Form&#160;S-4</span> was declared effective by the SEC.&#160;As a result SAM became an SEC registrant on July&#160;25, 2023. On July&#160;27, 2023, SAM common stock was listed for trading on the New&#160;York Stock Exchange. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">2023 Operating Environment </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Since 2020, Surf Air has been incurring expenses to support the development of the technology of its digital platform with the aim of providing a delightful, premium flying experience and Surf Air expects these development expenses to continue to be incurred. Additionally, Surf Air is developing hybrid-electric and electric powertrain technologies with its commercial partners to electrify existing fleets and new aircraft. As a result, Surf Air expects to incur significant costs in the future to support development of this technology. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Beginning in early 2020, the effects and potential effects of the global <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> pandemic, including, but not limited to, its impact on general economic conditions, trade and financing markets, changes in customer behavior with regard to air mobility services, and continuity in business operations created significant uncertainty for Surf Air. Surf Air has seen some recovery in <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> flights from 2021 through the third quarter of 2023, however Surf Air&#8217;s business has been and will continue to be affected by many changing economic and other conditions beyond Surf Air&#8217;s control, including global events that affect travel behavior. Surf Air has experienced inflationary pressures, which have materially increased Surf Air&#8217;s costs for aircraft fuel, wages and benefits and other goods and services critical to its operations during 2022 and 2023 and believes perceived recessionary risks may impact 2023 results. For example, perceived recessionary risks may cause companies and individuals to reduce travel for either professional or personal reasons, and drive higher prices in the supply chain Surf Air relies upon. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As such, the extent to which global events and market inflationary impacts will affect our financial condition, liquidity and future results of operations is uncertain. Given the uncertainty regarding the length of these factors, Surf Air cannot reasonably estimate their impact on its future results of operations, cash flows or financial condition. Surf Air continues to actively monitor its financial condition, liquidity, operations, suppliers, industry and workforce. As Surf Air does not currently, and does not intend in the foreseeable future to, enter into any transactions to hedge fuel costs, or otherwise fix labor costs, Surf Air will continue to be fully exposed to fluctuations in prices of material operating costs. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Key Operating Measures of Surf Air </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition to the data presented in our consolidated financial statements, we use the following key operating measures commonly used throughout the air transport industry to evaluate our business, measure our performance, develop financial forecasts and make strategic decisions. The following table summarizes key operating measures for each period presented below, which are unaudited. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(1)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:left">Scheduled Flight&#160;Hours represent actual flight time from takeoff through landing that were flown in the period and excludes departures for maintenance or repositioning events. This metric only measures flight&#160;hours for flights that generated scheduled revenue and does not include flight&#160;hours for flights that generated <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> revenue. </p></td></tr></table>

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:left"><span style="white-space:nowrap">On-Demand</span> Flights represent the number of flights that generate <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> revenue taken by customers on Surf Air aircraft or third-party operated aircraft during the period. </p></td></tr></table>

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:left">Scheduled Passengers represent the number of passengers flown during the period for scheduled service. </p></td></tr></table>

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:left">Headcount represents all full-time and part-time employees at the end of the period. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(5)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:left">Scheduled Departures represent the number of takeoffs in the period, agnostic of operator of Surf Air&#8217;s services and excludes departures for maintenance or repositioning events. This metric only measures takeoffs that generated scheduled revenue and does not include takeoffs that generated <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> revenue. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Components of Surf Air&#8217;s Results of Operations </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The key components of our results of operations include: </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Revenue </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air&#8217;s revenue is comprised of <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> trips and scheduled flight services. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="white-space:nowrap">On-Demand</span> Revenue </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">On-demand</span> service allows customers to book an individual flight on routes specified by the customer. Customers can purchase single flights or prepaid, dollar based, credits. Single flights are paid for at booking. Flight credits are paid upon purchase and applied at booking. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company utilizes FAA certified independent third-party air carriers in the performance of its charter flights on Surf Air aircraft or on aircraft operated by those air carriers. The Company evaluates whether it is a principal or an agent in contracts involving more than one party by assessing whether it controls the flight services before they are transferred to its customers. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company acts as the principal when it controls the services by directing third-party air carriers and operators to provide services to customers on its behalf. The Company controls the services when it is primarily responsible for fulfillment of the flight services obligation to the customer and has pricing discretion. In these arrangements, revenue recognized is the gross amount of the contract consideration paid by customers. When the Company is not primarily responsible for the fulfillment of the flight services, it acts as an agent and therefore recognized revenue is net of amounts paid to third-party air carriers and operators that provide the services. The majority of the <span style="white-space:nowrap">On-Demand</span> revenue was recognized on a gross basis. Customers purchase prepaid credits for <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> services, and the revenue derived from these prepaid credits is recognized when the trip is flown. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Scheduled Revenue </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Scheduled revenue is derived from membership subscriptions, principally relating to two main categories of membership subscriptions: AYCF and PAYF. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">AYCF membership subscriptions allow members to book unlimited flights over the contract service term (monthly or annually). The membership fee includes the subscription and single seat fees. AYCF membership fees are billed monthly in advance, and revenue is recognized on a <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">month-to-month</span></span> basis over the service term. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">PAYF membership subscriptions allow members to purchase single use vouchers for travel on Surf Air&#8217;s scheduled routes. Vouchers sold in a package generally expire twelve&#160;months after the purchase date. Vouchers are nonrefundable, not exchangeable for cash, and may not be used for other services. Revenue is recognized for the membership fee and the purchase of vouchers, based on the pattern of voucher usage, or at expiration, whichever comes first. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">75 </p>

</div></div>



<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>



<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Cost of Revenue, exclusive of depreciation and amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Cost of revenue consists of expenditures directly related to delivering services and related facility costs. Service delivery costs are primarily comprised of fees paid to the independent third-party air carriers operating both scheduled flight services and <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> services when Surf Air is acting as the principal in the arrangement. Additionally, cost of revenue includes all personnel costs for member services and ground concierge staff. Facility costs represent leases and operating costs for stations throughout the scheduled service network. Cost of revenues excludes depreciation and amortization. We anticipate that these costs will fluctuate in absolute dollars over time and as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of our business. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Technology and Development </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Technology and development expense consists of personnel and other costs related to technology development and management efforts, including costs for third-party development resources. Technology and development efforts are focused on enhancing the ease of use and functionality of existing software platforms, as well as the development of new products and services. Technology and development costs are expensed as incurred, except to the extent that such costs are associated with <span style="white-space:nowrap">internal-use</span> software development that qualifies for capitalization. Technology and development expense excludes amortization of capitalized costs. We anticipate that these costs will fluctuate in absolute dollars over time due to the anticipated investment in software platforms. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Sales and Marketing </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sales and marketing expense consists primarily of personnel and other costs to support sales and marketing efforts. Personnel costs includes commissions, salaries, and related benefits. Additionally, sales and marketing expense includes expenses associated with promotions of services, advertising, and brand initiatives. We anticipate that these costs will fluctuate in absolute dollars over time and as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of our business. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">General and Administrative </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">General and administrative expense consists of personnel related costs for all business administrative functions. Additionally, stock-based compensation costs are included in this category for all personnel. Furthermore, professional fees, headquarter rents, and other corporate related expenses are reflected in this category. We expect our general and administrative expenses to increase in absolute dollars over time and to fluctuate as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of our business, and additional costs associated with becoming a public company. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Depreciation expense consists primarily of depreciation of furniture, fixtures, and leasehold improvements. Amortization expense consists of amortization of capitalized software development costs and trademarks. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other income/(expense) primarily consists of interest expense, changes in fair value of financial instruments, gain on extinguishment of debt and other <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operating</span> costs. We expect these expenses to fluctuate in absolute dollars over time with the market or changes in timing and nature of debt costs. Convertible notes, SAFEs, and warrants will be converted at listing and no longer require fair value measurement. The estimated fair values of these financial liabilities were determined utilizing the Probability-Weighted, Expected Return Method and is considered a Level&#160;3 fair value measurement. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">76 </p>

</div></div>

Surf Air conducted 533 <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights during the second quarter of 2023 compared to 403 <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights during the second quarter of 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights was driven by increases in marketing efforts for our <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> product and service strategy growth. In addition, price per trip increased during the second quarter of 2023 compared to the second quarter of 2022, primarily driven by a shift in customer preference to more expensive aircraft to service charter trips in 2023. </p>

The decrease was primarily attributable to a decline in our membership subscription base. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Cost of Revenue, exclusive of depreciation and amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Cost of revenue increased by $1.1&#160;million, or 19%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase was due to the number of charter flights increasing from 533 for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023 compared to 403 in the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. This increase was partially offset by lower third party carrier costs as a result of prepayment programs with preferred carriers during the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Technology and Development </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Technology and development expenses increased by $0.1&#160;million, or 14%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase was due to research and development costs to develop hybrid-electric technology. Surf Air expects continued increases in expenses in order to support the development of its hybrid-electric and electric powertrain technologies. With the completion of the Company&#8217;s direct listing, Surf Air expects development expenses to significantly increase contingent upon the successful consummation of contemplated financings through the SPA with GEM. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Sales and Marketing </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sales and marketing expenses increased by $0.8&#160;million, or 70%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in sales and marketing was primarily due to increased marketing expenses of $0.4&#160;million related to building brand awareness for the Company&#8217;s public listing, and a concerted effort to grow the <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> product offering, requiring increased salesforce and related commissions of $0.4&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">General and Administrative </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">General and administrative expenses decreased by $0.2&#160;million, or 2%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The decrease in general and administrative expenses was driven by a decrease in stock-based compensation expense of $3.6&#160;million. This decrease was partially offset by an increase in legal expenses of $2.7&#160;million, and an increase in professional service expenses of $0.7&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">After June&#160;30, 2023, and prior to the Company&#8217;s direct listing, the Company&#8217;s board of directors determined that the remaining vesting requirements applicable to previously granted executive equity awards had been satisfied, in connection with the Company&#8217;s direct listing. This will result in the recognition of $21.8&#160;million in previously unrecognized stock-based compensation expense during the third quarter of 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Depreciation and amortization expenses were flat period over period, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other expense, net increased from $5.7&#160;million for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022 to other expense, net of $31.4&#160;million for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023. In addition, we incurred a loss of $0.4&#160;million from the conversion of term and promissory notes during the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023 compared to a gain of $4.0&#160;million during the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Net Loss </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in net loss from the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022 compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, is primarily attributable to an increase in fair value of financial instruments of $21.0&#160;million, an increase in other expenses due to loss from term and promissory note conversions of $4.3&#160;million, an increase in sales and marketing expense of $0.8&#160;million, an increase in cost of revenue of $1.1&#160;million, and an increase in interest expense of $0.4&#160;million. Adjusted EBITDA is a supplemental measure of Surf Air&#8217;s performance that is not required by, or presented in accordance with, U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Adjusted EBITDA is not a measurement of Surf Air&#8217;s financial performance under U.S.&#160;GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) or any other performance measure derived in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Surf Air&#8217;s calculation of this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure may differ from similarly titled <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> measures, if any, reported by other companies. This <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measures may be calculated differently from, and therefore may not be directly comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air presents Adjusted EBITDA because it considers this measure to be an important supplemental measure of its performance and believes it is frequently used by securities analysts, investors, and other interested parties in the evaluation of companies in its industry. Management believes that investors&#8217; understanding of Surf Air&#8217;s performance is enhanced by including this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure as a reasonable basis for comparing its ongoing results of operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air calculates Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) adjusted for depreciation and amortization, interest expense, income tax expense, stock-based compensation, changes in fair value of financial instruments, and transaction costs. </p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">On-demand</span> revenue increased by $3.0&#160;million, or 44%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. Surf Air conducted 987 <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights during the first six&#160;months of 2023 compared to 796 <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights during the first six&#160;months of 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights was driven by increases in marketing efforts for our <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> products and other service offerings. In addition, price per trip increased during the first six&#160;months of 2023 compared to the first six&#160;months of 2022, primarily driven by a shift in customer preference to more expensive aircraft to service charter trips in 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Scheduled revenue decreased by $0.6&#160;million, or 24%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The decrease was primarily attributable to a decline in our membership subscription base. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Cost of Revenue, exclusive of depreciation and amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Cost of revenue increased by $2.4&#160;million, or 22%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase was due to the number of charter flights increasing to 987 in the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023 from 796 for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Technology and Development </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Technology and development expenses increased by $0.2&#160;million, or 12%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase was due to research and development costs to develop hybrid-electric technology. Surf Air expects continued increases in expenses in order to support the development of its hybrid-electric and electric powertrain technologies. With the completion of listing, Surf Air expects development expenses to significantly increase contingent upon the successful consummation of contemplated financings through the SPA with GEM. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Sales and Marketing </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sales and marketing expenses increased by $1.1&#160;million, or 47%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in sales and marketing was primarily due to a concerted effort to grow the <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> product offering, requiring increased salesforce and related commissions of $0.7&#160;million. Additionally, increased marketing and filming expenses related to building brand awareness for the Company&#8217;s public listing of $0.4&#160;million in the first six&#160;months of 2023 contributed to the increase. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">General and Administrative </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">General and administrative expenses were flat period over period, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. A decrease in stock-based compensation expense of </p>

$7.2&#160;million was offset by increases in professional service fees, including audit and legal expenses related to the Company&#8217;s public listing, of $6.0&#160;million. In addition, travel expenses and property and other taxes increased by $0.2&#160;million and $0.5&#160;million, respectively. Lastly, there was an increase in dues and subscriptions related to the Company&#8217;s public listing of $0.2&#160;million period over period. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">After June&#160;30, 2023, and prior to the Company&#8217;s direct listing, the Company&#8217;s board of directors determined that the remaining vesting requirements applicable to previously granted executive equity awards had been satisfied, in connection with the Company&#8217;s direct listing. This will result in the recognition of $21.8&#160;million in previously unrecognized stock-based compensation expense during the third quarter of 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Depreciation and amortization expenses were flat period over period, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other expense, net increased from $5.1&#160;million for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022 to other expense, net of $39.9&#160;million for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023. This was the result of increases in fair value of SAFE Notes of $23.5&#160;million, derivative liabilities of $8.5&#160;million, and conversion of certain convertible notes to preferred shares of $0.8&#160;million. In addition, we incurred a loss of $0.4&#160;million from the conversion of term and promissory notes during the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023 compared to a gain of $6.0&#160;million during the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. These were offset by a change in fair market value of certain convertible notes causing an unrealized gain of $3.0&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Net Loss </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in net loss from the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022 compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, is primarily attributable to an increase in fair value of financial instruments expense of $28.2&#160;million, a decrease in gain on extinguishment of debt of $6.3&#160;million, an increase in sales and marketing of $1.1&#160;million, and an increase in cost of revenue of $2.4&#160;million. These items were offset by an increase of $2.4&#160;million in revenue. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Adjusted EBITDA </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following table presents a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to net loss for each of the periods indicated. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Operating Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, net cash used in operating activities was $20.6&#160;million, driven by a net loss of $65.1&#160;million, partially offset by $2.8&#160;million in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> stock based compensation expenses, $38.5&#160;million in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> changes in fair value of financial instruments, $1.0&#160;million in accounts payable and accrued expenses, deferred revenue of $1.0&#160;million, depreciation and amortization of $0.5&#160;million, $0.4&#160;million increase in loss on extinguishment of debt, and $0.3&#160;million in accounts receivable and other current assets. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, net cash used in operating activities was $15.5&#160;million, primarily driven by a net loss of $29.4&#160;million, and a gain on extinguishment of debt of $6.0&#160;million. This was partially offset by $9.9&#160;million in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> stock based compensation expenses, and $10.3&#160;million in changes in fair value of financial instruments. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in operating activities increased period over period by $5.2&#160;million, driven by a $35.7&#160;million increase in net loss, and a decrease in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> stock-based compensation expense of $7.2&#160;million. These were partially offset by an increase of $28.2&#160;million in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> changes in fair value of financial instruments, an increase in loss on extinguishment of debt of $6.3&#160;million, an increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses of $2.1&#160;million, an increase in accounts receivable and other current assets of $0.8&#160;million, and an increase in deferred revenue of $0.3&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Investing Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023 and the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, net cash used in investing activities was driven by $0.3&#160;million and $0&#160;million, respectively, of property and equipment costs and software development costs. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Financing Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, net cash provided financing activities was $23.2&#160;million, primarily from proceeds from borrowings due to related parties of $16.5&#160;million, proceeds from borrowings of SAFE notes of $3.7&#160;million, and issuance of convertible preferred shares of $3.0&#160;million. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">83 </p>

These increases were partially offset by a reduction in proceeds from borrowings of SAFE and convertible notes of $14.4&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Results of Surf Air&#8217;s Operations for the&#160;Years Ended December&#160;31, 2022 and 2021 </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following table sets forth our consolidated statements of operations data for the&#160;years ended December&#160;31, 2022 and 2021 (in thousands, except percentages): </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; border-top:3.00px double #000000">&#160;</p></td>
<td>&#160;</td></tr>
</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">On-demand</span> revenue increased by $9.5&#160;million, or 147%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. Surf Air conducted 1,093 <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights in 2021, which were </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">84 </p>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>



<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
recognized as a combination of gross and net revenue. Surf Air conducted 1,696 <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights during 2022, which were recognized as revenue on a gross basis. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In 2022, Surf Air acted as the principal for <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> charter flights as we are primarily responsible for fulfillment of the obligation specified in the contract and had the authority to direct the key components of the service, and accordingly revenue recognized was the gross amount of the transaction. In 2021, the majority of the <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> revenue was recognized on a gross basis. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The comparative increase in <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> revenue was driven by the new <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> product and service strategy that drove increased demand in 2022 and gross revenue recognition. <span style="white-space:nowrap">On-demand</span> revenue also increased as a result of increased pricing due to rising fuel costs. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Scheduled revenue decreased by $1.0&#160;million, or 19%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. Surf Air flight&#160;hours decreased from 3,469 to 2,524, or 27%, from 2021 to 2022. In the second quarter of 2022, Surf Air transitioned to a new independent Part&#160;135 operator, requiring a reduction in scheduled offerings. The transition reduced second and third quarter 2022 scheduled flights due to delays in FAA processes and conformity of the Surf Air fleet onto the new operator&#8217;s certificate. Surf Air has completed conformity of its fleet to the new operator and scheduled flight levels resumed in late fall of 2022. Decreases in flight&#160;hours flown were offset by positive impacts from increased pricing of the AYCF product. The increase was driven by increased pricing in 2022 as the introductory pricing of $999 per month in 2021 for the AYCF product was no longer offered in 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Cost of Revenue, exclusive of depreciation and amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Cost of revenue increased by $10.3&#160;million, or 71%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. The increase was primarily due to increased third party operator pricing driven by increases in fuel costs. Additionally, the new <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> product and service strategy drove gross recognition of costs. This was offset by a slight decrease in cost of revenue for the scheduled service driven by lower flight&#160;hours. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Technology and Development </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Technology and development expenses increased by $0.3&#160;million, or 11%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. The increase was due to research and development costs for hybrid technology. Surf Air expects to incur significant costs in the future to support development of its powertrain technology. Surf Air expects development expenses to increase following the completion of the listing and Surf Air&#8217;s successful consummation of additional financings. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Sales and Marketing </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Sales and marketing expenses increased by $1.4&#160;million, or 38%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. The increase in sales and marketing was primarily due to a new <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-demand</span> product launch requiring increased salesforce and related commissions, and growth marketing investment to drive growth. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">General and Administrative </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">General and administrative expenses increased by $14.0&#160;million, or 61%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. The increase in general and administrative expenses was primarily driven by increases in stock-based compensation expense of $9.3&#160;million and increases in labor-related costs of $2.4&#160;million. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">85 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Depreciation and amortization were flat period over period. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other income/(expense) increased by $21.0&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. This increase was driven by an increase in fair value of financial instruments of $27.6&#160;million, driven mainly by the overall value of the Company and the expected value of conversion or redemption of financial instruments, consisting of convertible notes of $12.3&#160;million, SAFEs of $12.8&#160;million, preferred stock and warrants of $2.5&#160;million. The fair values of the convertible notes, preferred stock warrant liabilities, and SAFEs were based on the values of the notes, warrants, and derivatives upon conversion due to the weighted probability associated with certain events, which in the Company&#8217;s case, would be the sale of the Company or becoming a public company. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Significant unobservable inputs used in the valuation models as of December&#160;31, 2022 and 2021 included public listing probability, SPAC probability, lack of marketability, discount rates used in the sale scenario for debt instruments, discount rates used in the public listing scenario, discount rates used in the SPAC scenario and probability weight volatility. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The probability of a public listing increased significantly from 2021, due to the completion of required PCAOB audits, the filing of an <span style="white-space:nowrap">S-1,</span> and strides in public readiness efforts. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">These increases were offset by $5.3&#160;million in gains on extinguishment of debt related to the conversion of a term note to a SAFE and settlements of vendor payables for equity, and a decrease in interest expense of $1.5&#160;million driven by term notes that were converted to convertible notes. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Net Loss </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in net loss from the year ended December&#160;31, 2021, to December&#160;31, 2022, is primarily attributable to an increase in fair value of financial instruments of $27.6&#160;million, an increase in stock-based compensation expense of $9.3&#160;million, an increase in labor-related costs of $2.4&#160;million, and an increase in cost of revenue of $10.3&#160;million. These items were offset by an increase of $8.5&#160;million in revenue and $5.3&#160;million in gains on extinguishment of debt. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> Financial Measures </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air uses Adjusted EBITDA to identify and target operational results which is beneficial to management and investors in evaluating operational effectiveness. Adjusted EBITDA is a supplemental measure of Surf Air&#8217;s performance that is not required by, or presented in accordance with, U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Adjusted EBITDA is not a measurement of Surf Air&#8217;s financial performance under U.S.&#160;GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) or any other performance measure derived in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Surf Air&#8217;s calculation of this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure may differ from similarly titled <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> measures, if any, reported by other companies. This <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measures may be calculated differently from, and therefore may not be directly comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air presents Adjusted EBITDA because it considers this measure to be an important supplemental measure of its performance and believes it is frequently used by securities analysts, investors, and other interested parties </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">86 </p>

During June&#160;2023, the Company made $0.1&#160;million in payments to cure these defaults. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The airline industry and the Company&#8217;s operations are cyclical and highly competitive. The Company&#8217;s success is largely dependent on the ability to raise debt and equity capital, increase its membership base, increase passenger loads, and continue to expand into regions profitably throughout the United&#160;States. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern is dependent upon its ability to raise additional capital and to maintain revenues and generate profit from operations. The Company has funded its operations and capital needs primarily through the net proceeds received from the issuance of various debt instruments, convertible securities and preferred and common share financing arrangements. A significant amount of funding to date has been provided by entities affiliated with an officer and <span style="white-space:nowrap">co-founder</span> of the Company. The Company is evaluating strategies to obtain the additional funding for future operations. These strategies may include, but are not limited to, obtaining additional equity financing, issuing additional debt or entering into other financing arrangements, restructuring of operations to grow revenues and decrease expenses. There can be no assurance that the Company will be successful in achieving its strategic plans or that new financing will be available to the Company in a timely manner or on acceptable terms, if at all. If the Company is unable to raise sufficient financing when needed or events or circumstances occur such that the Company does not meet its strategic plans, the Company will be required to take additional measures to conserve liquidity, which could include, but are not necessarily limited to, reducing certain spending, altering or scaling back development plans, including our key strategic plans to equip regional airline operations with hybrid electric aircraft and reducing funding of capital expenditures, which would have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations, cash flows and ability to achieve its intended business objectives. These factors raise substantial doubt about the Company&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. The Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements do not include any adjustments to reflect the possible future effects on the recoverability and classification of assets or the amounts and classification of liabilities that may result from the outcome of this uncertainty. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">See the section entitled &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">Risk Factors</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;&#8212;</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;Risks Related to Surf Air&#8217;s and Southern&#8217;s Financial Position</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;&#8212;</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;There is substantial doubt about Surf Air&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. Surf Air will need additional financing to execute its business plan, to fund its operations and to continue as a going concern</span>&#8221; and &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">Risk Factors</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;&#8212;</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;Risks Related to SAM&#8217;s Financial Position and Capital Requirements</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;&#8212;</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;Surf Air has previously defaulted on its debt and other obligations and there can be no assurance that SAM will be able to fulfill its obligations under any current or future indebtedness it may incur</span>.&#8221; </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company&#8217;s prospects and ongoing business activities are subject to the risks and uncertainties frequently encountered by companies in new and rapidly evolving markets. changes in consumer and business behavior, pandemic fears, market downturns and restrictions on business and individual activities, which created significant volatility in the global economy and has led to reduced economic activity particularly in the air travel industry. Due to enhanced virtual meeting and teleconferencing technology that has been adopted throughout the <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> pandemic, more people are meeting over virtual meeting platforms than in person, which reduces the need for transportation. Specifically, <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> related disruption in air travel has led to a decrease in membership sales, flight cancellations and significant operational volatility contributing to Surf Air defaulting on certain debt arrangements and amending the terms and conditions of certain debt arrangements, in order to meet liquidity needs. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air&#8217;s capital expenditures in 2022 and the first six&#160;months of 2023 were limited to immaterial purchases and internally developed software. margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The consolidated financial statements of Surf Air are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United&#160;States of America (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">U.S.</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;GAAP</span>&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Use of Estimates </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The preparation of the consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S.&#160;GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements, and the reported amounts of income and expense during the reported period. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Our management believes that the accounting estimates listed below are those that are most critical to the portrayal of our financial condition and results of operations, and that require management&#8217;s most difficult, subjective and complex judgments in estimating the effect of inherent uncertainties. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Share-Based Compensation </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air accounts for the issuance of ordinary share options, restricted share units (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">RSUs</span>&#8221;), restricted share purchase agreements (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">RSPAs</span>&#8221;) and restricted share grant agreements (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">RSGAs</span>&#8221;) in its consolidated financial statements based on the grant date fair value of the awards. Issuances of RSPAs with promissory notes are accounted for as share options and are measured based on the grant date fair value of the option. Surf Air estimates the fair value of the share options using the Black-Scholes option pricing model. The grant date fair value of share-based awards with service-only conditions is recognized as expense on a straight-line basis in the consolidated statement of operations over the requisite service period, which is generally the vesting period ranging from 12 to 48&#160;months. Forfeitures are recorded as they occur. For awards with performance conditions, Surf Air records compensation expense on a graded-vesting basis when it is deemed probable that the performance condition will be met. For awards with market conditions, the effect of the market conditions is reflected in the fair value measurement and expense, recognized on a graded-vesting basis, and is not reversed to the extent that the market condition is not achieved. Additionally, awards granted to <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-employees</span> are accounted for using their grant date fair value and are accounted for in the same manner as awards granted to employees. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">91 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Determining the fair value of share-based awards requires judgment. Surf Air&#8217;s use of the Black-Scholes option pricing model requires the input of subjective assumptions, including the fair value of Surf Air&#8217;s ordinary shares underlying the option award, the expected term of the option, the expected volatility of Surf Air&#8217;s ordinary shares, risk-free interest rates and the expected dividend yield of Surf Air&#8217;s ordinary shares. The assumptions used in Surf Air&#8217;s option pricing model represent management&#8217;s best estimates. These estimates involve inherent uncertainties and the application of management&#8217;s judgment. If factors change and different assumptions are used Surf Air&#8217;s share-based compensation expense could be materially different in the future. Surf Air estimates volatility using the historical volatility of common shares of similar entities. The expected term of options granted represents the period for which the options are expected to be outstanding and is estimated based on an average between the contractual and vesting terms of the awards. The risk-free interest rate is derived from the U.S.&#160;Treasury yield curve in effect at the date of grant. Surf Air has not declared or paid dividends to date and does not anticipate declaring dividends. As such, the dividend yield has been estimated to be zero. Surf Air&#8217;s assumptions may change for future grants. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Because there is no public market for Surf Air&#8217;s ordinary shares, Surf Air&#8217;s board of directors has determined the fair value of the ordinary shares by considering a number of objective and subjective factors including the results of third-party valuations, Surf Air&#8217;s actual operating and financial performance, market conditions and performance of comparable publicly traded companies, developments and milestones in Surf Air, the likelihood of achieving a liquidity event and transactions involving Surf Air&#8217;s preferred or common shares, among other factors. The effect of these inherent uncertainties make share-based compensation arrangements more difficult, subjective and complex to estimate. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Fair Value Measurements </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air&#8217;s financial results reflect a significant number of debt and equity transactions that must be fair valued. Fair value is defined as the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">market participants on the measurement date. Valuation techniques used to measure fair value must maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs. The assumptions used in Surf Air&#8217;s valuation models represent management&#8217;s best estimates. These estimates involve inherent uncertainties and the application of management&#8217;s judgment. If factors change and different assumptions are used, Surf Air&#8217;s results could reflect material fluctuation in Changes in fair value of financial instruments carried at fair value, net on the Consolidated Statement of Operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Fair value measurements are based on a fair value hierarchy, based on three levels of inputs, of which the first two are considered observable and the last unobservable, which are the following: </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air measures the fair value of certain long-lived assets including finite-lived intangible assets on a nonrecurring basis, when such assets are required to be written down to fair value if impaired. Such fair values are classified within Level&#160;3 of the fair value hierarchy, as the valuations contain significant unobservable inputs, including assumptions of the present value of future cash flows, the use of these assets, as well as estimated disposition value. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air&#8217;s convertible securities and Simple Agreements for Future Equity (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">SAFE</span>&#8221;) notes are carried at fair value<span style="font-style:italic">.</span> SAFE notes are financial instruments whereby an investor provides an investment into Surf Air, and the note is subsequently converted into a preferred equity security at a discount to the price paid by other investors when and if a preferred equity is issued through a qualifying capital raise. Due to certain provisions included in the agreements for these instruments, they are classified as liabilities. Additionally, Surf Air elected the fair value option for certain convertible notes and SAFE notes, which requires them to be remeasured to fair value each period. If factors change and different assumptions are used, Surf Air&#8217;s results could reflect material fluctuation in Changes in fair value of financial instruments carried at fair value, net on the Consolidated Statements of Operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Income Taxes </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The determination of tax strategies and positions, along with accounting for related income taxes requires interpretation of various federal and state tax policies and assessment of the likelihood of various outcomes. Management believes that accounting for income taxes requires difficult, subjective and complex judgments and defenses. Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the consolidated financial statements carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases and tax credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the&#160;years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The likelihood of realizing the tax benefits related to a potential deferred tax asset is evaluated, and a valuation allowance is recognized to reduce that deferred tax asset if it is more likely than not that all or some portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are calculated at the beginning and end of the period. The change in the sum of the deferred tax asset, valuation allowance and deferred tax liability during the period generally is recognized as a deferred tax expense or benefit. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in operations in the period that includes the enactment date. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air determines whether a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return is to be recognized in the consolidated financial statements when it is more likely than not, based on the technical merits, that the position will be sustained upon examination. The amount recognized is subject to estimation and management judgment with respect to the likely outcome of each uncertain tax position. The amount that is ultimately sustained for an individual uncertain tax position or for all uncertain tax positions in the aggregate could differ from the amount recognized. For tax positions meeting the more likely than not threshold, the tax amount recognized in the consolidated financial statements is reduced by the largest benefit that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority. Surf Air recognizes interest and penalties accrued related to unrecognized tax benefits, if any, in its income tax expense in the accompanying Consolidated Statement of Operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">JOBS Act </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Surf Air currently qualifies as an &#8220;emerging growth company&#8221; under the JOBS Act. Accordingly, Surf Air has elected to use the extended transition period for complying with any new or revised financial accounting standards provided pursuant to Section&#160;7(a)(2)(B)&#160;of the Securities Act. Surf Air&#8217;s utilization of these transition periods may make it difficult to compare our financial statements to those of <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-emerging</span> growth companies and other emerging growth companies that have opted out of the transition periods afforded under the JOBS Act. </p>
