 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:center" id="toc462861_12">SOUTHERN&#8217;S MANAGEMENT&#8217;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">References in this section to &#8220;Southern&#8221; refers to Southern Airways Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries. Unless otherwise indicated, all dollar amounts are set forth in thousands, except share and per share data. </span></p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">The following discussion and analysis is intended to help the reader understand Southern&#8217;s results of operations and financial condition. This discussion and analysis is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, the section entitled &#8220;Unaudited Pro Forma Condensed Combined Financial Information&#8221; and Southern&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included elsewhere in this prospectus. Some of the information contained in this discussion and analysis or set forth elsewhere in this prospectus, including information with respect to Southern&#8217;s plans and strategy for Southern&#8217;s business, includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Southern&#8217;s actual results may differ materially from management&#8217;s expectations as a result of various factors, including but not limited to those discussed in the sections entitled &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; and &#8220;Special Note&#160;Regarding Forward-Looking Statements.&#8221; </span></p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Overview of Southern&#8217;s Business </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Palm Beach, Florida, Southern is a commuter airline currently serving 40 U.S.&#160;cities across six U.S.&#160;time zones. Southern operates a fleet of 50 aircraft, including the Cessna Caravan, the King Air Super 200, Pilatus <span style="white-space:nowrap">PC-12,</span> Tecnam Traveler and the Saab 340B.&#160;As of June&#160;30, 2023, Southern is the largest passenger operator of Cessna Caravans in the United&#160;States by scheduled departures. It served over 400,000 customers with nearly 75,000 departures in 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern has seen substantial growth resulting from its commitment to the individual passenger, recognized in its company mantra, &#8220;Every Passenger, Every Day, Every Flight&#8221;. Southern operates the largest commuter airline in the United&#160;States by scheduled departures, safely carrying hundreds of thousands of passengers per year. Southern, along with its Hawaiian brand, Mokulele Airlines, operates over 200 daily departures stretching from Nantucket to Hawaii. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern provides both seasonal and full-year scheduled passenger air transportation service with select routes subsidized by the U.S.&#160;federal government under the Essential Air Service (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">EAS</span>&#8221;) program. The EAS program was created to ensure small communities in the United&#160;States can maintain a minimum level of scheduled air services. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern earns revenue from sales of tickets for scheduled passenger flight service, as well as charter flights and tours. These sales are generally paid for via credit card. Southern also earns revenue generated by third-party travel booking sites and travel agencies. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additionally, Southern earns revenue from various ancillary services such as baggage fees, reservation change fees and pet <span style="white-space:nowrap">(carry-on)</span> fees. These types of fees are standard within the aviation industry. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">2023 Operating Environment </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Beginning in early 2020, effects and potential effects of the global <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> pandemic, including, but not limited to, its impact on general economic conditions, trade and financing markets, changes in customer behavior with regard to air mobility services and continuity in business operations created significant uncertainty for Southern. The spread of <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> also disrupted the manufacturing, delivery and overall supply chain of aircraft manufacturers and suppliers and has led to a global decrease in aircraft sales in markets around the world. Southern may be impacted by fluctuations in new and used aircraft markets as it acquires aircraft to supply capacity for its business. Initially in 2020, the <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> pandemic caused a decrease in demand for Southern&#8217;s air mobility services, the impact of which is more fully described in the sections entitled, &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">Risk Factors</span>&#8221; and &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">&#8212;</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;Liquidity and Capital Resources.</span>&#8221; </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">94 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern has seen partial recovery in demand from 2021 through the second quarter of 2023, however Southern&#8217;s business has been and will continue to be affected by many changing economic and other conditions beyond Southern&#8217;s control, including global events that affect travel behavior. Additionally, Southern has experienced inflationary pressures, which have materially increased Southern&#8217;s costs for aircraft fuel, wages and benefits and other goods and services critical to its operations during 2022 and 2023 and believes perceived recessionary risks will continue to impact 2023 results. For example, perceived recessionary risks may cause companies and individuals to reduce travel for either professional or personal reasons, and drive higher prices in the supply chain Southern relies upon. As Southern does not currently, and does not intend in the foreseeable future to, enter into any transactions to hedge fuel costs, or otherwise fix labor costs, Southern will continue to be fully exposed to fluctuations in prices of material operating costs. In addition, Southern incurred greater than expected losses and negative cash flows from operating activities during the second quarter of 2023 due to inefficient aircraft utilization, primarily caused by an underutilization of pilots and a shortage of maintenance personnel and critical aircraft components, which, in aggregate, have challenged the Company&#8217;s ability to serve its customers as desired and, in turn, cover expenses. In June&#160;2023, Southern finalized the sale of an aircraft with a transaction price of $1.4&#160;million, of which $1.2&#160;million was used to repay principal and accrued interest on a portion of a loan with Clarus Capital&#160;I Funding LLC, including payment of certain transaction-related expenses. The Company received the remaining $0.2&#160;million in cash and recognized a gain of approximately $0.2&#160;million from the sale of the aircraft. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As such, the extent to which global events and market inflationary impacts will affect Southern&#8217;s financial condition, liquidity and future results of operations is uncertain. Given the uncertainty regarding the length of these factors, Southern cannot reasonably estimate their impact on its future results of operations, cash flows or financial condition. Southern continues to actively monitor its financial condition, liquidity, operations, suppliers, industry and workforce. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Key Operating Measures of Southern </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition to the data presented in Southern&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, Southern uses the following key operating measures commonly used throughout the air transport industry to evaluate its business, measure its performance, develop financial forecasts, and make strategic decisions. The following table summarizes Southern&#8217;s key operating measures for each period presented below, which are unaudited. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>



<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Components of Southern&#8217;s Results of Operations </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The key components of Southern&#8217;s results of operations include: </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Revenues </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern&#8217;s revenues are comprised of passenger ticket sales on scheduled routes, chartered flights and other services. Southern&#8217;s scheduled service offerings include market-based and subsidized routes, which consist of Southern&#8217;s EAS routes and other routes funded through government subsidies. The chartered service offering reflects individual flights on Southern&#8217;s fleet of aircraft. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Passenger Revenue </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Direct passenger revenue consists of single seat tickets for scheduled flight service. Tickets are refundable within 24&#160;hours of purchase for flights scheduled to take place more than one week out, or when flights are changed, interrupted, or otherwise canceled. Direct passenger sales revenues are recognized when the flights are completed or when tickets expire (generally within one year from the date of purchase). </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Essential Air Services (&#8220;EAS&#8221;) and Other Subsidy Revenue </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">EAS revenue is derived from operating scheduled passenger flight service on certain routes, which are subsidized by the U.S.&#160;DOT under its EAS program. The EAS program was enacted in 1978 to ensure small communities in the United&#160;States can maintain a minimum level of scheduled air services. Contracts under this program are typically two to four&#160;years in duration and include commitments to fly a specific number of times annually to each location. Revenue from EAS subsidies is recognized monthly. Revenue from sales of tickets on flights subsidized by the EAS program is recognized in direct passenger revenue and is recognized when the flights are completed. Other subsidy revenue represents subsidies received by Marianas for providing scheduled route services for Saipan, Tinian, Rota and Guam under the Incentive Agreement with the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. Due to the termination of the Incentive Agreement, Southern ceased serving the Mariana Islands as of April&#160;1, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Charter Revenue </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Charter service allows customers to book an entire aircraft that is not part of scheduled service and is tailored to the needs of the customer. The customer will specify the date, time and route for the flight purchased. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern utilizes <span style="white-space:nowrap">FAA-certified</span> independent third-party air carriers in the performance of charter flights on Southern&#8217;s own fleet of aircraft or on aircraft operated by those independent third-party air carriers. Southern evaluates whether it is a principal or an agent in contracts involving more than one party by assessing whether it controls the flight services before they are transferred to its customers. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern acts as the principal when it controls the services by directing third-party air carriers and operators to provide services to customers on its behalf. Southern controls the services when it is primarily responsible for fulfillment of the flight services obligation to the customer and has pricing discretion. In these arrangements, revenue recognized is the gross amount of the contract consideration paid by customers. When Southern is not primarily responsible for the fulfillment of flight services, it acts as an agent and therefore recognized revenue is net of amounts paid to third-party air carriers and operators that provide the services. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Revenue </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other revenue is derived from various ancillary services related to baggage fees, reservation change fees and pet <span style="white-space:nowrap">(carry-on)</span> fees. These types of fees are standard within the aviation industry and are earned when the services are performed at the time of travel. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">96 </p>

</div></div>



<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%" />
<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>



<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Costs and expenses consist of the following components: </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Maintenance, materials and repairs </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Maintenance, materials and repairs expense consists primarily of engine overhauls, mandatory periodic inspections, routine and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-routine</span> repair and general maintenance monitoring expense. Southern anticipates that these costs will fluctuate in absolute dollars over time and as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of its business. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern&#8217;s depreciation expense consists primarily from depreciation on Southern&#8217;s owned aircraft. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Fuel </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft fuel expense consists of aircraft fuel usage expense, along with certain fees for <span style="white-space:nowrap">re-fueling</span> services. Southern anticipates that these costs will fluctuate in absolute dollars over time and as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of its business and changes in market prices. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Airport-Related Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Airport-related expenses consist of aircraft landing fees, hangar rental, aircraft parking fees, terminal rent, as well as other airport-related charges. Southern anticipates that these costs will fluctuate in absolute dollars over time and as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of its business. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Rent </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft rent is comprised of aircraft leases classified as operating leases. The associated lease payments over the term of the leases are recognized either on a straight-line or hourly usage basis. Southern anticipates that these costs will fluctuate in absolute dollars over time and as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of its business. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Salaries, Wages, and Benefits </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Salaries, wages, and benefits consist of all payroll-related costs relating to all personnel. Southern expects its payroll expenses to increase in absolute dollars over time and to fluctuate as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of Southern&#8217;s business. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other operating expenses consist primarily of charges relating to the operation of <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-wage</span> related customer service costs, passenger ticket reservation system, insurance expenses, utilities expense, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-aircraft</span> rent expense, legal and other professional fees, and marketing expense inclusive of advertising costs. Southern expects its other operating expenses to increase in absolute dollars over time and to fluctuate as a percentage of revenue due to the anticipated growth of its business and increased marketing investments. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> income/(expense) primarily consists of interest expense and other <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operating</span> items. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">97 </p>

</div></div>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Passenger ticket revenue decreased $0.8&#160;million, or 8%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. Southern flew 117,670 passengers across its network in the second quarter of 2022. In the second quarter of 2023, Southern flew 97,344 passengers, a 17% decrease in passengers compared to the prior comparative period. The primary reason for the decrease is due to the availability of aircraft impacted by maintenance and added downtime due to supply chain issues in sourcing critical spare parts. </p>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>



<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in EAS and other subsidy revenue of $3.4&#160;million, or 43%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, was driven by the addition of six new routes under the EAS program of $3.8&#160;million, which was offset by reduced scheduled departures on existing EAS routes of $0.4&#160;million due to the availability of aircraft impacted by maintenance and added downtime due to supply chain issues in sourcing critical spare parts. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in charter revenue of $0.3&#160;million, or 32%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, was driven by increased trips at Southern&#8217;s Hawaii based charter operations due to focusing on providing route services for construction crews, school events, and leisure travel. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The decrease in other revenue of $0.1&#160;million, or 10%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, was driven by a decrease in scheduled passengers, and associated fees, of 17% period over period. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Maintenance, Materials, and Repairs </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Maintenance, materials, and repairs increased by $0.3&#160;million, or 23%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. Flight&#160;hours operated by Southern increased from 17,155 in the first three&#160;months of 2022 to 17,650 in first three&#160;months of 2023, or a 3% increase. The increase in flight&#160;hours drove an increase in costs on aircraft engine monitoring, engine overhauls, mandatory timed periodic inspections, and routine and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-routine</span> repairs by $0.3&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Depreciation and amortization increased by $0.2&#160;million, or 37%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in depreciation and amortization expenses was primarily attributable to aircraft additions during the second half of 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Fuel </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft fuel expenses decreased by $1&#160;million, or 22%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The decrease in aircraft fuel was attributable to the decrease in fuel prices of 24% or $1&#160;million offset by higher flight&#160;hours of 3% or $0.1&#160;million. Fuel prices are expected to continue to be subject to volatility in the near term. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Airport Related Expense </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Airport related expenses increased by $0.2&#160;million, or 16%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in airport related expenses on airport rent, hangar rent, other station expenses, and landing fees were primarily attributable to six EAS routes awarded by the DOT since the first quarter of 2022. This was offset by a decrease in fight departures of 19,283 in the second quarter of 2022 to 16,832 in the second quarter of 2023, or 13% decrease in departures. Southern does not expect to incur airport related expenses related to the Marianas routes in the future, as the flight operations related to Marianas were terminated at the beginning of April&#160;2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Rent </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft rent expenses increased by $0.4&#160;million, or 21%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase was primarily related to aircraft engine reserves on leased aircraft. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">99 </p>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>



<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Salaries, Wages, and Benefits </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Salary, wages, benefits expenses increased by $1.5&#160;million, or 20%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. With the increase in flight&#160;hours, salary, wages, and benefit expenses for pilots increased $0.5&#160;million, and customer care increased $0.8&#160;million. The remaining increase in salary, wages and benefits of $0.1&#160;million was for corporate office departments not associated with flight&#160;hours. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Operating Expense </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other operating expenses increased $1.1&#160;million, or 25%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. This consisted of increased pilot travel, training, and ongoing drug screening costs of $0.6&#160;million, increased insurance costs of $0.2&#160;million, and increased facility charges of $0.1&#160;million. Higher corporate travel costs of $0.1&#160;million also contributed to the increase in other operating expenses. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> expense increased by $0.1&#160;million, or 29%, for the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operating</span> expenses was due to $0.4&#160;million in interest expense on borrowings for purchased aircraft, offset by gain on sale of an aircraft of $0.3&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Net Income/(Loss) attributable to common shareholders </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net loss attributable to common shareholders increased from the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022 compared to the three&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, primarily attributable to an increase in relative prices for aircraft repairs and maintenance of $0.3&#160;million, an increase in salaries, wages, and benefits of $1.5&#160;million, offset by lower fuel prices of $1.0&#160;million as discussed above. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> Financial Measures </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern uses Adjusted EBITDA to identify and target operational results which is beneficial to management and investors in evaluating operational effectiveness. Adjusted EBITDA is a supplemental measure of Southern&#8217;s performance that is not required by, or presented in accordance with, U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Adjusted EBITDA is not a measurement of Southern&#8217;s financial performance under U.S.&#160;GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) or any other performance measure derived in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP, or as an alternative to cash flows from operating activities as a measure of Southern&#8217;s liquidity. Southern&#8217;s calculation of this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure may differ from similarly titled <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> measures, if any, reported by other companies. This <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measures may be calculated differently from, and therefore may not be directly comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern presents Adjusted EBITDA because it considers this measure to be an important supplemental measure of its performance and believes it is frequently used by securities analysts, investors, and other interested parties in the evaluation of companies in its industry. Management believes that investors&#8217; understanding of Southern&#8217;s performance is enhanced by including this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure as a reasonable basis for comparing its ongoing results of operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern calculates Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) adjusted for depreciation and amortization, interest expense, income tax expense and incentive income from the Marianas joint venture. </p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Passenger ticket revenue increased $1.2&#160;million, or 7%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. Southern&#8217;s average per ticket price rose 17% from $82 in the first half of 2022 to $96 in the first half of 2023 generating $2.6&#160;million. This was partially offset by an 8% decrease in passengers of $1.4&#160;million period over period. The primary reason for the decrease is due to the availability of aircraft due to maintenance and added downtime due to supply chain issues in sourcing critical parts for aircraft repairs and maintenance. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in EAS and other subsidy revenue of $6.8&#160;million, or 46%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, was driven by the addition of six new routes under the EAS program, during the second half of 2022 and the first half of 2023, of $6.4&#160;million and an increase in scheduled departure revenue on existing routes of $0.3&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in charter revenue of $0.7&#160;million, or 34%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, was driven by increased trips at Southern&#8217;s Hawaii based charter operations due to focusing on providing route services for construction crews, school events, and leisure travel. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in other revenue of $0.1&#160;million, or 4%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, was driven by managing reservations for other carriers, interline fees, and automobile rental fees. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Maintenance, Materials, and Repairs </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Maintenance, materials, and repairs increased by $1.3&#160;million, or 52%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. Flight&#160;hours operated by Southern increased from 32,054 in the first half of 2022 to 35,315 in first half of 2023, or a 10% increase. The increase in flight&#160;hours drove an increase in costs on aircraft engine monitoring, engine overhauls, mandatory timed periodic inspections, and routine and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-routine</span> repairs by $1.3&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Depreciation and amortization increased by $0.6&#160;million, or 52%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in depreciation and amortization expenses was primarily attributable to aircraft additions during the second half of 2022. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">102 </p>

</div></div>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Fuel </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft fuel expenses increased by $0.2&#160;million, or 3%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in aircraft fuel was attributable to higher flight&#160;hours of 10% or $0.7&#160;million offset by a decrease in fuel prices of 7% or $0.5&#160;million. Fuel prices are expected to continue to be subject to volatility in the near term. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Airport Related Expense </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Airport related expenses increased by $0.7&#160;million, or 37%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in airport related expenses on airport rent, hangar rent, other station expenses, and landing fees were primarily attributable to six EAS routes awarded by the DOT since the first quarter of 2022, as well as the addition of the Marianas route in the second half of 2022. Offset by the decrease in fight departures of 36,370 in the first half of 2022 to 34,502 in the first half of 2023, or 5% decrease in departures. Southern does not expect to incur airport related expenses related to the Marianas routes in the future, as the flight operations related to Marianas were terminated at the beginning of April&#160;2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Rent </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft rent expenses increased by $0.7&#160;million, or 17%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase was primarily related to aircraft engine reserves on leased aircraft of $0.5&#160;million and new leased aircraft of $0.1&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Salaries, Wages, and Benefits </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Salary, wages, benefits expenses increased by $4.1&#160;million, or 31%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. With the increase in flight&#160;hours, salary, wages, and benefit expenses for pilots increased $1.2&#160;million, customer care increased $1.7&#160;million, and maintenance increased $0.3&#160;million. The Marianas joint venture increased salary, wages, and benefits by $0.4&#160;million. The remaining increase in salary, wages and benefits of $0.5&#160;million was for corporate office departments not associated with flight&#160;hours. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Operating Expense </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other operating expenses increased $2.4&#160;million, or 29%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. This consisted of increased pilot travel, training, and ongoing drug screening costs of $0.9&#160;million, increased insurance costs of $0.5&#160;million, increased passenger reaccommodating of $0.4&#160;million, and increased facility charges of $0.2&#160;million. Higher corporate travel costs of $0.2&#160;million also contributed to the increase in other operating expenses. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> expense increased by $0.4&#160;million, or 76%, for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, compared to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022. The increase in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operating</span> expenses was due to $0.9&#160;million in interest expense on borrowings for purchased aircraft, offset by gain on sale of an aircraft of $0.3&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Net Income/(Loss) attributable to common shareholders </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net loss attributable to common shareholders increased from the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022 to the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, and was primarily attributable to an increase in relative prices for aircraft repairs and maintenance of $1.3&#160;million and aircraft rent of $0.7&#160;million as discussed above. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> Financial Measures </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern uses Adjusted EBITDA to identify and target operational results which is beneficial to management and investors in evaluating operational effectiveness. Adjusted EBITDA is a supplemental measure of Southern&#8217;s performance that is not required by, or presented in accordance with, U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Adjusted EBITDA is not a measurement of Southern&#8217;s financial performance under U.S.&#160;GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) or any other performance measure derived in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP, or as an alternative to cash flows from operating activities as a measure of Southern&#8217;s liquidity. Southern&#8217;s calculation of this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure may differ from similarly titled <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> measures, if any, reported by other companies. This <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measures may be calculated differently from, and therefore may not be directly comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern presents Adjusted EBITDA because it considers this measure to be an important supplemental measure of its performance and believes it is frequently used by securities analysts, investors, and other interested parties in the evaluation of companies in its industry. Management believes that investors&#8217; understanding of Southern&#8217;s performance is enhanced by including this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure as a reasonable basis for comparing its ongoing results of operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern calculates Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) adjusted for depreciation and amortization, interest expense, income tax expense and incentive income from the Marianas joint venture. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following table presents a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to net loss for each of the periods indicated. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Operating Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, net cash used in operating activities was $1.9&#160;million, primarily driven by a $2.6&#160;million increase in operating lease expense, an $0.6&#160;million increase in accounts receivables, and a $0.4&#160;million decrease in accounts payable and other liabilities. This was partially offset by an increase in deferred revenue of $1.3&#160;million, and a decrease in prepaid expenses and other current assets of $0.3&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, net cash generated in operating activities was $0.4&#160;million, primarily driven by a $2.1&#160;million increase in deferred revenue, $1&#160;million in cash from operations including <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> items, and an increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses of $0.8&#160;million. Partially offset by $1.8&#160;million of operating leases, prepaid expenses and other current assets of $1.6&#160;million, and $0.1&#160;million in accounts receivables. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in operating activities increased period over period by $2.4&#160;million, primarily driven by an increase in operating losses including <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cash</span> items of $1&#160;million, accounts payable and accrued expenses of $1.3&#160;million, operating leases of $0.7&#160;million, accounts receivables of $0.5&#160;million, and deferred revenue of $0.8&#160;million. This was partially offset by increases of $1.9&#160;million in prepaid expenses and other current assets. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Investing Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, net cash generated in investing activities was $0.3&#160;million from proceeds from sale of assets $1.4&#160;million, offset by $1.1&#160;million in purchases of property and equipment (aircraft, spare parts, ground equipment, and leasehold improvements). </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, net cash used in investing activities was $17.7&#160;million from purchases of property and equipment (aircraft, spare parts, ground equipment, and leasehold improvements) of $13.5&#160;million and the acquisition of MUA (Multi Aero) of $4.2&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash generated in investing activities increased period over period by $17.9&#160;million primarily due to purchases of property and equipment (aircraft, spare parts, ground equipment, and leasehold improvements) of $12.4&#160;million and the acquisition of MUA (Multi Aero) of $4.2&#160;million in six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022 without similar events in the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Financing Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2023, net cash provided by financing activities was $1.3&#160;million, driven by $2.7&#160;million in borrowings from related parties and $1.3&#160;million in collateralized borrowings. This was partially offset by $2.3&#160;million in payments of long-term debt and $0.4&#160;million in repayments of long-term debt on related parties. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2022, net cash provided in financing activities was $15.4&#160;million, driven by $16.9&#160;million borrowings from long-term debt and $1&#160;million in proceeds from Marianas. This was offset by $2.1&#160;million in repayment of long-term debt and $0.3&#160;million repayments of long-term debt on related parties. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in financing activities decreased period over period by $14&#160;million, driven by $16.9&#160;million borrowings from long-term debt and $1&#160;million in proceeds from Marianas. This was offset by $2.7&#160;million in borrowings of long-term debt and $1.3&#160;million in collateralized borrowings. </p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Passenger revenue increased $13.2&#160;million, or 51%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. Southern flew 324,634 passengers across its network in 2021. In 2022, Southern flew 442,893 passengers, a 36.4% increase in passengers compared to the prior comparative period. Prices for passenger tickets increased slightly based on the mix of routes and introduction of higher priced routes. The increase in passenger revenue is primarily driven by the increase in flight demand generated by relaxing of COVID restrictions from 2021 to 2022. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in EAS and other subsidy revenue of $6.9&#160;million, or 27%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021, was driven by an increase in new routes under the EAS program of $4.7&#160;million, contract rate increases of $1.6&#160;million, and $0.6&#160;million from other subsidy routes. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in charter revenue of $1.9&#160;million, or 63%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021, was driven by the lessening of <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> restrictions in 2022, which increased demand for charter flights by $1.7&#160;million, as well as rate increases of $0.2&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The increase in other revenue of $0.9&#160;million, or 29%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021, was driven by the increase in passengers of 36% period over period. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Operating Expenses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Maintenance, Materials, and Repairs </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Maintenance, materials, and repairs increased by $2.4&#160;million, or 79%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. Flight&#160;hours operated by Southern increased from 54,274 in 2021 to 68,316 in 2022, or a 26% increase. The increase in flight&#160;hours drove the increase in costs&#160;on aircraft engine monitoring, engine overhauls, mandatory timed periodic inspections, and repairs by $1.1&#160;million. Rate increases on&#160;aircraft engine monitoring, engine overhauls, mandatory timed periodic inspections, and repairs contributed to the increase in the amount of $1.0&#160;million.&#160;Furthermore, there was an increase of $0.3&#160;million in repair part freight costs due to rising fuel prices, and the increase in costs of materials due to supply chain issues following <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19.</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Depreciation and Amortization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Depreciation and amortization increased by $1.4&#160;million, or 90%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. The increase in depreciation and amortization expenses was primarily attributable to aircraft additions during late 2021 and throughout 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Fuel </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft fuel expenses increased by $7.4&#160;million, or 89%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. The increase in aircraft fuel was attributable to the increase in flight&#160;hours of 26% and rising fuel prices. Southern expects elevated fuel prices to continue in 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Airport Related Expense </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Airport related expenses increased by $1.5&#160;million, or 48%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. Landing fees increased $0.5&#160;million primarily due to rate increases compared to the prior comparative period, and after hour and call out fees increased $0.5&#160;million primarily due to increased flight volume. Hangar and airport rent increased $0.6&#160;million due to rate increases and additional locations. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Aircraft Rent </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Aircraft rent expenses increased by $0.9&#160;million, or 12%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. In late 2021 and 2022, Southern added ten leased aircraft to the fleet and no aircraft were removed from the fleet in 2021 or in 2022. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">107 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Salaries, Wages, and Benefits </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Salary, wages, benefits expenses increased by $7.8&#160;million, or 37%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. With the increase in flight&#160;hours salary, wages, and benefit expenses for pilots increased $2.8&#160;million, customer care increased $2.0&#160;million, and maintenance increased $1.0&#160;million, resulting from increases in pay rates and higher salaried new employees. The Marianas joint venture increased salary, wages, and benefits by $0.4&#160;million. The remaining increase in salary, wages and benefits of $1.6&#160;million was for corporate office departments not associated with flight&#160;hours. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">CARES Act </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During 2020 and 2021 collectively, because of the negative impact of the <span style="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</span> pandemic, Southern was awarded a total grant of $22.3&#160;million to support ongoing payroll and ongoing operations through the PPP and PSP.&#160;In 2021, $11.1&#160;million was recognized as income and none remained to be recognized in 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Other Operating Expense </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other operating expenses increased $6.3&#160;million, or 51%, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year December&#160;31, 2021. This consisted of increased pilot travel, training, and ongoing costs of $1.7&#160;million, costs associated with the addition of Marianas of $0.9&#160;million, increased insurance costs of $1.1&#160;million, increased facility charges of $0.4&#160;million and increased reservation system costs of $0.7&#160;million, all of which supported increased flight demand. Higher merchant fees of $0.5&#160;million, professional fees of $0.5&#160;million, and corporate travel costs of $0.5&#160;million also contributed to the increase in other operating expenses. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> Income/(Expense) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operating</span> expense increased by $0.9&#160;million, or 134%, for the year&#160;ended December&#160;31, 2022, compared to the year ended December&#160;31, 2021. The increase in <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operating</span> expense was due to $1&#160;million in interest expense on borrowings for purchased aircraft, offset by <span style="white-space:nowrap">start-up</span> costs for the Marianas of $0.2&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Net Income/(Loss) attributable to common shareholders </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The change in net income to net loss attributable to common shareholders from the year ended December&#160;31, 2021 to December&#160;31, 2022, is primarily attributable to the absence of $11.1&#160;million of PSP/PPP grant funding, $3.8&#160;million in operating losses that were the result of rising fuel prices and <span style="white-space:nowrap">start-up</span> costs for the Marianas joint venture and new routes, and an increase of $1.0&#160;million in interest to finance new aircraft leases. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> Financial Measures </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern uses Adjusted EBITDA to identify and target operational results which is beneficial to management and investors in evaluating operational effectiveness. Adjusted EBITDA is a supplemental measure of Southern&#8217;s performance that is not required by, or presented in accordance with, U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Adjusted EBITDA is not a measurement of Southern&#8217;s financial performance under U.S.&#160;GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) or any other performance measure derived in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP, or as an alternative to cash flows from operating activities as a measure of Southern&#8217;s liquidity. Southern&#8217;s calculation of this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure may differ from similarly titled <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> measures, if any, reported by other companies. This <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</span> financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measures may be calculated differently from, and therefore may not be directly comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern presents Adjusted EBITDA because it considers this measure to be an important supplemental measure of its performance and believes it is frequently used by securities analysts, investors, and other interested parties in the evaluation of companies in its industry. Management believes that investors&#8217; understanding of Southern&#8217;s performance is enhanced by including this <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial measure as a reasonable basis for comparing its ongoing results of operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern calculates Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) adjusted for depreciation and amortization, interest expense, income tax expense, incentive income from the Mariana joint venture and PPP/PSP grants. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following table presents a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to net income (loss) for each of the periods indicated. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the year ended December&#160;31, 2021, net cash generated by operating activities was $11.0&#160;million, driven by $9.6&#160;million in PPP and PSP grants and $2.8&#160;million in cash from operating profits. This was partially offset by $1.9&#160;million in prepaid expenses and other assets. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in operating activities decreased year over year by $9.2&#160;million, driven by $9.6&#160;million in PPP and PSP grants received in 2021 with none in 2022, an increase of $4.1&#160;million in operating leases, an increase of $1.6&#160;million prepaid expenses and other assets, $1.0&#160;million less in operating profits, and $0.8&#160;million from accounts receivable. Offsets were primarily driven by increases of $7.4&#160;million in accounts payable. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Investing Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, net cash used in investing activities was $23.1&#160;million, driven by $18.9&#160;million in purchases of property and equipment (aircraft, spare parts, ground equipment, and leasehold improvements) and $4.2&#160;million in the acquisition of Multi Aero. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the year ended December&#160;31, 2021, net cash used in investing activities was $6.3&#160;million, driven by purchases of property and equipment (aircraft, spare parts, ground equipment and leasehold improvements). </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash used in investing activities used period over period increased by $16.9&#160;million driven by a $12.6&#160;million increase in purchases of property and equipment (aircraft, spare parts, ground equipment, and leasehold improvements) and $4.2&#160;million in the acquisition of Multi Aero. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Cash Flow from Financing Activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the year ended December&#160;31, 2022, net cash generated in financing activities was $17&#160;million, $19.7&#160;million in proceeds from borrowings of long-term debt and $1.3&#160;million in borrowings under factoring agreement, offset by $3.9&#160;million in repayment of debt and $0.1&#160;million in repayment of finance capital lease obligations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the year ended December&#160;31, 2021, net cash used in financing activities included $0.8&#160;million in repayment of debt and $0.3&#160;million in repayment of finance capital lease obligations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net cash generated by financing activities increased period over period by $18.2&#160;million, driven by an increase of $19.7&#160;million in proceeds from borrowings of long term debt, an increase of $1.3&#160;million in borrowings under factoring agreement and an increase of $0.1&#160;million in repayment of finance capital lease obligations, offset by the repayment of debt of $3.0&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Liquidity and Capital Resources </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern incurred greater than expected operating losses and negative cash flows from operating activities during the second quarter of 2023 due to inefficient aircraft utilization, primarily caused by an underutilization of pilots and a shortage of maintenance personnel and critical aircraft components, which, in aggregate, have challenged Southern&#8217;s ability to serve its customers as desired and, in turn, cover expenses. Previously forecasted strategies to alleviate these challenges have been unsuccessful in the full deployment of Southern&#8217;s fleet with the Company seeing an increased cancellation rate well above historical averages and previous forecasts, particularly during the second quarter of 2023. This has resulted in an accelerated decline in revenue expectations in the second quarter of 2023, coupled with increasing costs associated with rescheduling pilots and flight personnel to active service areas to mitigate the flight schedule disruptions. Although Southern continues to focus on mitigating these challenges, they are expected to continue to impact financial results in the coming&#160;months. Southern&#8217;s success going forward is dependent on the ability to achieve a high level of aircraft and crew utilization, increase flight services and the number of passengers flown, and ready access to capital to fund operations and planned growth. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of June&#160;30, 2023, Southern had approximately $1.1&#160;million in cash and available liquidity. In addition to continued actions to reduce costs, and effectively utilize assets and crews, Southern is evaluating strategies to obtain additional funding for future operations. These strategies may include, but are not limited to, obtaining additional equity financing, issuing additional debt or entering into other financing arrangements, and restructuring of operations to efficiently utilize aircraft and pilots, grow revenues and decrease expenses. There can be no assurance that Southern will be successful in achieving its strategic plans, that new financing will be available to Southern in a timely manner or on acceptable terms, if at all. If Southern is unable to raise sufficient financing when needed or events or circumstances occur or such that Southern does not meet its strategic plans, Southern may be required to take additional measures to enhance and conserve and increase liquidity, which could include, but not necessarily limited to, increasing ticket prices, additional reductions to spending, selling of aircraft, altering or scaling back operational footprint, which may have a material adverse effect on Southern&#8217;s financial position, results of operations, cash flows, and ability to achieve its intended business objectives. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">These factors raise substantial doubt about Southern&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. Southern&#8217;s consolidated financial statements do not include any adjustments to reflect the possible future effects on the recoverability and classification of liabilities that may result from the outcome of this uncertainty. See the section entitled &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">Risk Factors</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;&#8212;</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;Risks Related to Surf Air&#8217;s and Southern&#8217;s Financial Position</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;&#8212;</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;There is substantial doubt about Southern&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. Southern will need additional financing to execute its business plan, to fund its operations and to continue as a going concern</span>&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The accompanying consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United&#160;States of America (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">U.S.</span><span style="font-style:italic"></span><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;GAAP</span>&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Use of Estimates </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The preparation of the consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S.&#160;GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements, and the reported amounts of income and expense during the reported period. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern&#8217;s management believes that the accounting estimates listed below are those that are most critical to the portrayal of Southern&#8217;s financial condition and results of operations, and that require management&#8217;s most difficult, subjective, and complex judgments in estimating the effect of inherent uncertainties. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Income Taxes </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The determination of tax strategies and positions, along with the accounting for related income taxes, require interpretation of various federal and state tax policies and assessment of the likelihood of various outcomes. Management believes that accounting for income taxes requires difficult, subjective, and complex judgments and defenses. Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the consolidated financial statements carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases and tax credit carry forwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the&#160;years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The likelihood of realizing the tax benefits related to a potential deferred tax asset is evaluated, and a valuation allowance is recognized to reduce that deferred tax asset if it is more likely than not that all or some portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are calculated at the beginning and end of the period. The change in the sum of the deferred tax asset, valuation allowance and deferred tax liability during the period generally is recognized as a deferred tax expense or benefit. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in operations in the period that includes the enactment date. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">111 </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern determines whether a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return is to be recognized in the consolidated financial statements when it is more likely than not, based on the technical merits, that the position will be sustained upon examination. The amount recognized is subject to estimation and management judgment with respect to the likely outcome of each uncertain tax position. The amount that is ultimately sustained for an individual uncertain tax position or for all uncertain tax positions in the aggregate could differ from the amount recognized. For tax positions meeting the more likely than not threshold, the tax amount recognized in the consolidated financial statements is reduced by the largest benefit that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority. Southern recognizes interest and penalties accrued related to unrecognized tax benefits, if any, in its income tax expense in the accompanying Consolidated Statement of Operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">JOBS Act </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Southern currently qualifies as an &#8220;emerging growth company&#8221; under the JOBS Act. Accordingly, Southern is provided the option to adopt new or revised accounting guidance either (i)&#160;within the same periods as those otherwise applicable to <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-emerging</span> growth companies or (ii)&#160;within the same time periods as private companies. Southern has elected to adopt new or revised accounting guidance within the same time period as private companies, unless Southern&#8217;s management determines it is preferable to take advantage of early adoption provisions offered within the applicable guidance. Southern&#8217;s utilization of these transition periods may make it difficult to compare its financial statements to those of <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-emerging</span> growth companies and other emerging growth companies that have opted out of the transition periods afforded under the JOBS Act. </p>
